label: high after unrewarded / a1 trials; at D2 high for a1->S2, low for a2->S1
terms: (phase == D1) * table(prev_action, {1: 1, 2: -1}) ;; (phase == GO) * table(prev_action, {1: 1, 2: -1}) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * (prev_reward == 0) ;; (phase == D2) * table(3*action+state, {4: 0, 5: 1, 7: -1, 8: 0.2}) ;; (tv("reward", -2) == 0) * (1 + (phase == D1))
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 6 is strongly phase-locked (D2 ~0.71, D1 ~0.36, GO ~0.19; timing R^2 0.70). Beyond timing, observed-only terms: at D1 (and weaker at GO) it is raised when the previous choice was a1 and lowered when it was a2 (weight ~0.16 D1, ~0.07 GO), and raised after an unrewarded previous trial (~0.17 D1, ~0.10 GO, ~0.07 D2); so it peaks after a1-unrewarded (+0.3) and dips after a2-rewarded (-0.2). At D2 it depends on this trial choice x reached state: high for a1->S2 rare (+0.19), low for a2->S1 rare (-0.25), near baseline for common transitions. An unrewarded trial two back adds a little. Long rewarded a1 streaks are over-predicted (actual activation low), the main remaining error. The model policy logit (choice) tracks it too (D1 residual rises with a1 preference; dev R^2 0.78 with choice terms) but the recorded set uses only observed cues. Value and hidden good state / since-reversal add little. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.74 (all ceiling 0.93, all observed 0.85).

issues: The claims check out. The terms reproduce test R^2 beyond timing of 0.744. The fitted weights match what the explanation states: D1 prev_action 0.157, GO 0.065; prev_reward==0 0.171 / 0.105 / 0.068 at D1 / GO / D2. In the profile, the D1 residual by previous trial is a1-u about +0.30 to +0.32 and a2-r about -0.19 to -0.21, as stated. The D2 choice x state residual is 5 (a1->S2) +0.189, 7 (a2->S1) -0.254, 4 -0.007 and 8 +0.040, which also matches.

The a1/a2 effect at D1 and GO is fit better by this trial's UPCOMING choice (future, though the agent computes it itself) than by the previous choice. Swapping prev_action for action gives test 0.797 against 0.739; using both gives 0.829. Adding the model's choice logit at D1 and GO gives test 0.867. So the unit mainly tracks the agent's current a1-vs-a2 preference. The label's 'after a1 trials' is only the observed stand-in for that. The explanation mentions the policy-logit link (dev 0.78) but not that the upcoming action alone beats prev_action.

The two-trials-back unrewarded term adds almost nothing: test 0.7391 without it, 0.7438 with it. History terms do not help either. a1-rewarded streak counts give 0.740, a 3-trial a1-rewarded streak indicator gives 0.741, prev_action at -2 and -3 gives 0.744, and a model-based predicted-choice term gives 0.743. So the acknowledged over-prediction on long rewarded a1 streaks is not fixable with simple observed history. It reflects the policy state.
Misses show no large systematic class. The mean error by phase is at most 0.013 in magnitude. The largest cell errors are about 0.07: GO after a1 S2 u +0.069 and D2 after a2 S1 u -0.065.

Full per-phase last-trial and trial-before lookup tables do not beat the claimed terms on test (0.716 to 0.740). The reported 'all observed' ceiling of 0.85 therefore seems hard to reach with additive observed terms (it may include tables that are future at D1/GO). This does not count against the label.
